title: Heuristic Origins — Daily Digest
content:
Purpose:
Quick running notes on how heuristics/provenance should behave for small/broken-signal records. This is a working brain-dump — not final. Use this to seed a formal guideline later.

High-level constraints I want to enforce:
- Preserve origin at a granular level: capture (source_system, ingestion_method, user_copy_paste_flag).
- Heuristics must be additive and reversible where possible (record both applied rule id and pre-transform snippet).
- When two heuristics conflict, prefer higher-precision rule (explicit mapping) over fuzzy normalization.

Immediate pain points observed this week:
1) SKU-ish tokens: mixed delims and trailing punctuation
   - examples: "X-12", "X12", "X_12.", "X12,". Our current merge rule collapses punctuation but loses variant semantics for vendor-specific prefixes (e.g., 'X_12' vs 'X12' are different vendors).
   - rough rule proposal: only collapse internal punctuation when vendor prefix matches known set (maintain vendor table). Otherwise keep original and add normalized field.

2) Dates with two-digit years: ambiguous century
   - examples: "03/04/05" could be 2005/2005? We have a bias toward 20xx for all modern datasets, but historical ingest (legacy ledger) uses 1900s.
   - approach: rely on ingestion source tag; if ingestion_source=="legacy-ledger" then prefer 19xx range, else 20xx. If unknown, mark as ambiguous and route to micro-adjudication.

3) Quoted blocks with embedded metadata
   - users paste emails with headers (From:, Sent:, etc.) and our parser sucks. Need a heuristic to detect copy/paste of full email and extract only body.
   - detection signal: presence of line-start tokens like "From:", long sequences of email-like addresses, and 'Sent:' lines. If detected, store raw_text and body_extracted, add provenance tag 'email-pasted'.

Micro-adjudication flow (sketch):
- Candidate sampled when: ambiguous_date || vendor-mismatch || conflicting-entity-maps || high-impact fields (PII, price) with low confidence.
- Sample size: start with 25 examples per rule per week. If error rate > 10%, escalate to 200 and create a rule PR.
- Quick adjudicator UI notes: show original text, normalized output, rule_id, and a one-click 'accept normalized / keep original / propose new'.

Heuristic registry idea (fields to capture per rule):
- rule_id (short slug)
- short_description (one line)
- signature_examples (3-5 strings)
- confidence_estimate (low/med/high)
- reversible (yes/no)
- last_touched (YYYY-MM-DD)
- owner (person/team)

Examples for registry entries (brain dump):
- rule_id: sku-collapse-basic
  short_description: remove internal punctuation for recognized vendor prefixes
  signature_examples: ["X-12","X_12","X12."]
  confidence_estimate: med
  reversible: yes
  owner: data-curation

- rule_id: date-two-digit-century-resolve
  short_description: bias two-digit years based on ingestion source
  signature_examples: ["03/04/05","12-31-99"]
  confidence_estimate: low
  reversible: yes
  owner: data-curation

Quick regex cheats (for my own use):
- SKU normalization (naive): s/^([A-Za-z0-9]+)[\-_,\. ]+([0-9]+)$/\1\2/  --> but add vendor whitelist check before applying.
- Email-paste detection: /^(From:|Sent:|To:).{0,80}$/mi  (also look for multiple @ tokens).
- Ambiguous date detection: / \d{1,2}[\-/]\d{1,2}[\-/]\d{2} /

Sampling heuristics for long-tail errors:
- Use stratified reservoir sampling keyed by (ingestion_source, rule_id) with an emphasis on low-frequency ingestion sources (weight +3x).
- For currency/price anomalies, sample by amount magnitude buckets (0-10, 10-100, 100-1k, 1k-10k, >10k) to ensure we catch formatting vs unit errors.

Conversation fragments / TODOs:
- @Noah: can you export the vendor prefix whitelist we discussed? I'll iterate on the sku-collapse-basic rule once I have it.
- Determine whether we keep both 'normalized_sku' and 'canonical_sku' or collapse into one. My leaning: keep both; canonical only after adjudication.
- @Sofia: quick UX ask — can the adjudication modal show the last 3 applied rules and timestamps? Means we can revert easily.

Open questions (need quick decisions):
- How many reversible transforms do we allow to stack before we lock a record for manual review? (2 vs 4?)
- Do we store pre-transform snippets inline, or in a separate audit blob? Tradeoff: inline increases record size; separate blob complicates queries.
- Should ambiguous_date automatically trigger a priority routing for enterprise customers? (Probably yes — higher SLA)

Sticky edge examples to test soon:
- "acct# 000-1234" vs "acct0001234" (do we treat dash as formatting only?)
- Mixed language tokens: "Café-Store, Calle 8" — lowercasing loses diacritics. Decision: prefer preserving unicode, add ascii-normalized field.

End-of-day quick action list:
- [ ] Draft minimal heuristic registry schema in Confluence (link above).
- [ ] Pull vendor prefix list from payments team (Noah).
- [ ] Add ambiguous_date sampling to adjudication queue (Sofia to wire UI).
- [ ] Add a small ETL job to persist pre-transform snippet for high-impact fields.

Notes-to-self (style):
- Keep examples short and representative.
- When writing rules later, include a 'rollback test' that applies the rule then attempts to reverse it on a held-out set.

Last thought: provenance matters more than normalization for debugging. If we can always answer "how did this value change and why" we save hours. Aim for small wins first (sku/date/email heuristics) and iterate.
